concordance-01.why: The main verb is past (m’a dit), so the présent shifts to the imparfait; aujourd’hui il va mieux shows that “being ill” was only true then.

concordance-02.why: With a past main verb, the passé composé of the original shifts to the plus-que-parfait (elle avait envoyé), and ce matin becomes le matin même.

concordance-03.why: In past reported speech the futur simple becomes the conditionnel présent (rappellerait); il ne l’a jamais fait shows it is all in the past.

concordance-04.why: A reported yes/no question takes si, not ce que or qu’est-ce que.

concordance-05.why: « Qu’est-ce qui s’est passé ? » is reported with ce qui (subject); qu’est-ce qui cannot be used in an indirect question.

concordance-06.why: Reporting an order: impératif → demander à qqn de + infinitif: Elle m’a demandé de la rappeler.

concordance-07.why: The time of speaking has changed, so in past reported speech demain becomes le lendemain (hier → la veille).

concordance-08.why: In past reported speech the futur proche becomes aller in the imparfait + infinitif: elle allait fermer.

concordance-09.why: An indirect question uses statement order — no est-ce que, no inversion: quand je pouvais visiter.

concordance-10.why: An imparfait in the original stays the same in past reported speech.

concordance-11.why: Reporting a past question: passé composé → plus-que-parfait; vouloir savoir si + statement order.

concordance-12.why: « Qu’est-ce que » becomes ce que in an indirect question (ce can’t be dropped), and the futur shifts to the conditionnel: ce que je ferais.
